result.message: Reviewed the submitted nan_to_num_ candidate (.best_kernel.py, sha256 bc15a973… = ledger round-3 solution and the subject under review) against the frozen catalog contract (definition.json / evaluation-contract.json / correctness.jsonl / timing.jsonl / oracle.py) and the round history and measurements in .ledger.json, optimize_definition_output.json and the review_tests artifacts. The candidate is a genuine self-contained Triton in-place pass: `run(A, nan=None, posinf=None, neginf=None)` mutates A's storage and returns A, matching `mutates: [A]` / `returns_alias_of: {out: A}` (definition.json:32-39); it uses no torch.ops/torch fallback, no host synchronization, no .item()/.cpu(), no environment mutation and no test-specific shapes or magic values (block sizes are dtype/size-driven). The saturating-clamp selection (element_size()==2 and posinf>=finfo.max and neginf<=finfo.min) is an algebraically valid simplification, but the graded set never exercises its complement: all correctness cases pass nan=0., posinf=None, neginf=None (oracle.py:43-44) and all timing inputs are plain randn with no NaN/±Inf (timing.jsonl:1-12), so the fast=False branch and the fp32-staged replacement values are unvalidated, and 6 of 18 'special' correctness cases (shape [1], numel<7) contain no special values at all because the edge-value injection is gated on numel>=7 (oracle.py:20-23; correctness.jsonl:1-2,7-8,13-14). Static review found no wrong-implementation measurement or reference-circularity issue; per the supplied evidence (evaluate.json / optimize_definition_output.json) the candidate passed 18/18 correctness and 12/12 timing with abs/rel error 0.0, and the ledger records 30/30 PASSED. The substantive code concerns are: (a) the cached direct Triton launcher bypasses Triton's per-call specialization checks (pointer alignment/divisibility) and is keyed only by (dtype, numel, fast) with no device key, so a second NPU could launch on device-0's cached stream; (b) reliance on private torch_npu/Triton launch internals with no guard at launch time, so a failure raises instead of using the documented fallback; (c) complex inputs silently no-op; (d) overlapping (expanded/stride-0) views silently succeed where the reference raises. Performance note (not a defect): in the authoritative final verification the delivered candidate is slower than the reference on all 12 timing workloads (geo_mean 0.6513; per-workload speedup ≈0.53-0.73, e.g. timing-3 0.0576 ms vs reference 0.0305 ms), so the PASSED status is a correctness gate, not a speedup over the baseline.
